trees.name: Sugar Maple
trees.fun_fact: A single tree can produce 10-20 gallons of sap per season.

trees.name: Eastern White Pine
trees.fun_fact: Can grow over 200 feet tall — the tallest conifer in eastern North America.

trees.name: Red Oak
trees.fun_fact: Acorns take two years to mature and are a keystone food for wildlife.

trees.name: American Beech
trees.fun_fact: Its smooth gray bark was historically used as a 'message board' by travelers.

trees.name: Paper Birch
trees.fun_fact: Indigenous peoples used its waterproof bark to build canoes.

trees.name: Live Oak
trees.fun_fact: Can live for over 500 years and spread wider than it is tall.

trees.name: Bald Cypress
trees.fun_fact: One of the few conifers that sheds its needles every fall.

trees.name: Southern Magnolia
trees.fun_fact: Its flowers can be up to 12 inches across and are among the oldest flowering plants.

trees.name: Loblolly Pine
trees.fun_fact: The most commercially important timber species in the southeastern US.

trees.name: Sweetgum
trees.fun_fact: Its spiky seed balls are nature's caltrops — painful to step on barefoot.

trees.name: Bur Oak
trees.fun_fact: Its thick bark makes it the most fire-resistant oak in North America.

trees.name: Eastern Cottonwood
trees.fun_fact: One of the fastest-growing trees in North America — up to 6 feet per year.

trees.name: Shagbark Hickory
trees.fun_fact: Its nuts were a primary food source for Native Americans for thousands of years.

trees.name: Black Walnut
trees.fun_fact: Produces juglone, a chemical that kills many nearby plants.

trees.name: American Elm
trees.fun_fact: Once lined nearly every Main Street in America before Dutch Elm Disease.

trees.name: Joshua Tree
trees.fun_fact: Not actually a tree — it's a giant member of the asparagus family.

trees.name: Palo Verde
trees.fun_fact: Its green bark photosynthesizes even after dropping its leaves.

trees.name: Arizona Sycamore
trees.fun_fact: Found only near desert streams — a true oasis indicator.

trees.name: Mesquite
trees.fun_fact: Its roots can extend over 150 feet deep to find water.

trees.name: Pinyon Pine
trees.fun_fact: Its edible pine nuts have been harvested by humans for over 10,000 years.

trees.name: Douglas Fir
trees.fun_fact: Not a true fir — it has its own genus. The cones have mouse-tail bracts.

trees.name: Western Red Cedar
trees.fun_fact: Called the 'Tree of Life' by Pacific Northwest tribes for its many uses.

trees.name: Sitka Spruce
trees.fun_fact: Its lightweight, strong wood was used to build WWII aircraft.

trees.name: Bigleaf Maple
trees.fun_fact: Its leaves can be over a foot wide — the largest of any maple.

trees.name: Pacific Madrone
trees.fun_fact: Sheds its bark to reveal smooth, red-orange wood underneath.

trees.name: Coast Redwood
trees.fun_fact: The tallest living organism on Earth at 380+ feet.

trees.name: Giant Sequoia
trees.fun_fact: The most massive single organism ever known — General Sherman weighs ~2.7M lbs.

trees.name: Valley Oak
trees.fun_fact: The largest North American oak, with canopies spreading over 100 feet.

trees.name: Monterey Cypress
trees.fun_fact: Naturally occurs in only two groves on the Monterey Peninsula.

trees.name: California Fan Palm
trees.fun_fact: The only palm native to the western US — found in desert oases.

trees.name: English Oak
trees.fun_fact: The Royal Navy was nicknamed 'The Wooden Walls' because ships were built from these.

trees.name: European Beech
trees.fun_fact: The word 'book' comes from the Old English 'bōc' meaning beech.

trees.name: Scots Pine
trees.fun_fact: The most widely distributed pine species in the world.

trees.name: Silver Birch
trees.fun_fact: A pioneer species — one of the first trees to colonize open ground.

trees.name: Horse Chestnut
trees.fun_fact: Kids in the UK play 'conkers' by swinging its seeds on strings.

trees.name: Banyan Tree
trees.fun_fact: A single tree in India covers over 5 acres with its aerial roots.

trees.name: Coconut Palm
trees.fun_fact: Coconuts can float for months and germinate after washing ashore.

trees.name: Kapok
trees.fun_fact: Maya believed it connected the underworld, earth, and heavens.

trees.name: Teak
trees.fun_fact: Contains natural oils that make it nearly impervious to rot and termites.

trees.name: Royal Poinciana
trees.fun_fact: Called 'flamboyant' — its red flowers make it one of the most colorful trees on Earth.

trees.name: Ginkgo
trees.fun_fact: A living fossil — unchanged for 200 million years. Survived the dinosaurs.

trees.name: Japanese Cherry
trees.fun_fact: Hanami, the tradition of viewing cherry blossoms, dates back over 1,000 years.

trees.name: Baobab
trees.fun_fact: Can store up to 32,000 gallons of water in its trunk.

trees.name: Rainbow Eucalyptus
trees.fun_fact: Its bark peels in strips to reveal neon green, blue, orange, and maroon wood.

trees.name: Dragon Blood Tree
trees.fun_fact: Bleeds red resin used as dye, medicine, and varnish for 2,000+ years.
